Very strong match. Let me now check a few other ear rot classes to rule them out, then view the remaining classes with budget.
Diplodia shows white/straw mold, Gibberella shows pink/red rot — both clearly don't match. Now I need to view 10 more classes to meet the 16-view budget.

- All leaf disease classes (Common Rust, Northern Leaf Blight, Gray Leaf Spot, Tar Spot, Goss's Wilt, Southern Rust, Stewart's Disease, Maize Dwarf Mosaic, Physoderma Brown Spot) are entirely irrelevant — wrong plant part and symptom type.
- Other ear rots (Diplodia = white/straw, Gibberella = pink/red, Fusarium = white/pinkish) don't match the olive-green coloration.

The test image shows a corn ear with localized olive-green powdery/dusty mold on the mid-section kernels, dark tip discoloration, and husks pulled back — an exact visual match for Aspergillus Ear Rot.
